summary: The Allama Iqbal Scholarships for Sri Lankan Students are run by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan under the Pak-Sri Lanka Higher Education Cooperation Programme. The programme spreads 1,000 awards over five years for Sri Lankan citizens to study at undergraduate, master's or doctoral level at top-ranked Pakistani universities. Fields are medicine, engineering, general science, social sciences, arts and humanities, and computing. The awards give the tuition fee, accommodation, study and books allowances and one return air ticket, and recipients must serve Sri Lanka after their studies.
eligibility_notes:
Only Sri Lankan citizens can apply. Dual nationals are not eligible.

Bachelor's level: GCE A-Level or an equivalent exam in the subjects the programme needs, with at least 60% marks. For Medicine the applicant needs pre-medical A-Level (or equivalent) with at least 65%. For Engineering the applicant needs pre-engineering A-Level (or equivalent) with at least 65%. HEC publishes a table that converts Sri Lankan grades into Pakistani marks: for the A-Level, A counts as 90, B as 75, C as 60, S as 45 and F as zero; for the O-Level, D counts as 90, C as 75, S as 60 and F is a fail.

Master's level: 16 years of education in relevant subjects, with 60% marks at graduate level.

Doctoral level: 18 years of education in a relevant subject, with a CGPA of 3.00 out of 4.00 at master's level. A research thesis at MS level is required.

The qualification must be obtained on or before the application deadline. After the award, successful candidates must provide an Equivalence Certificate from IBCC and HEC.

To apply on the HEC e-portal, the user manual says the applicant needs a valid email address, a profile picture, and a valid Sri Lankan passport or national identity number entered in the profile.

Teaching is in English; the pages name no language test. Recipients must serve Sri Lanka after completing their education in Pakistan. If the information given is found to be false or misrepresented, the scholarship can be ended at any stage. HEC strongly encourages women to apply.
age_experience_notes: The terms page sets a maximum age of 23 for BS programmes and 35 for graduate (master's) and doctoral programmes. The older user manual (January 2020) gives 22 for BS and 35 for MS and PhD, counted on the closing date; the terms page is the current one. No work experience requirement is stated for any level.
funding_summary: The pages name these components: the full tuition fee of the programme, an accommodation allowance, a study allowance, a books allowance and a one-time return air ticket. They give no amounts and do not say how many years the award is paid. The programme overview says that, of the 1,000 awards, 800 are full-support awards and 200 are partial awards. An earlier round's notice (2022) describes the partial award as tuition only and the full award as tuition, hostel, books and a maintenance allowance; the current pages do not repeat this split.
programmes_note: HEC names three field groups: Engineering Sciences, Basic and Natural Sciences, and Social Sciences. The Programs Offered list is more detailed. For BS it has five groups: Medical (MBBS); Engineering; General Science; Social Sciences, Arts and Humanities; and Computer Science. For MS and PhD it has ten groups each: Engineering; Computer Science and Information Technology; Mathematics and Statistics; Physical Sciences; Business and Management Sciences; Arts, Humanities and Languages; Social Sciences; Agriculture and Veterinary Sciences; Biological Sciences; and Medical Sciences. The subjects in each group are listed under each level. Engineering and Medicine have the higher 65% entry mark.
institutions_note:
HEC lists 11 participating engineering universities: NED University of Engineering and Technology (Karachi); NUST; Mehran University of Engineering and Technology (Jamshoro); University of Engineering and Technology Peshawar; University of Engineering and Technology Taxila; University of Engineering and Technology Lahore; COMSATS University Islamabad; Bahria University Islamabad; Air University Islamabad; University of Agriculture Faisalabad; and National Textile University Faisalabad.

It lists 26 general universities: International Islamic University Islamabad; Quaid-e-Azam University; Fatima Jinnah Women University; University of Agriculture Faisalabad; University of Peshawar; COMSATS University Islamabad; Bahria University Islamabad; Air University Islamabad; University of the Punjab; University of Sindh; PMAS Arid Agriculture University Rawalpindi; Institute of Management Sciences Peshawar; Sukkur IBA University; University of Agriculture Peshawar; Government College University Lahore; Bahauddin Zakariya University Multan; University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences Lahore; Institute of Space Technology; National College of Arts Lahore; NUML; Information Technology University Lahore; University of Education Lahore; Sindh Madressatul Islam University; University of Karachi; Karakorum International University; and BUITEMS.

The page adds that all public sector medical colleges and other renowned universities for the remaining disciplines also take part. HEC alone decides where each student is placed.

summary.detail: Undergraduate (BS) study at Pakistani universities, taught in English. Entry: GCE A-Level or equivalent in the required subjects with at least 60% marks; 65% in the pre-medical stream for Medicine and in the pre-engineering stream for Engineering. Maximum age 23. Five BS groups are offered.

Route and booking arrangements are not stated.

requirements.text: Online application form on the HEC e-portal for the Pak-Sri Lanka programme, with a registered account (Sri Lanka chosen as nationality, mobile number and verified email).
Profile picture uploaded in the applicant's profile.
Valid Sri Lankan passport number or Sri Lankan identity number entered in the National ID section of the profile.
Personal and educational documents uploaded to the profile; each file must be under 500 KB. Education details (Intermediate, GCE O/A level, bachelor's or master's) are entered in date order.
Research proposal, uploaded with the application form. The applicant also states the area of research or specialisation.
requirements.conditional_rule: Doctoral (PhD) applicants; MS applicants enter an area of research or specialisation

requirements.text: Equivalence Certificate from IBCC and HEC, supplied after the award.

application_steps.title: Create an account on the HEC e-portal
application_steps.detail: Register an account for the Pak-Sri Lanka programme, choose Sri Lanka as nationality, enter a mobile number and email, and verify the email with the code the system sends. A user manual is linked from the how-to-apply page.

application_steps.title: Complete your profile and upload documents
application_steps.detail: Enter personal and contact details and your Sri Lankan passport or identity number, upload a profile picture, and upload personal and educational documents (each file under 500 KB). Add degrees in date order.

application_steps.title: Fill in the application form and submit it
application_steps.detail: Choose BS, MS or PhD, then the category and subject, and answer the undertaking question with Yes (No stops the application). MS and PhD applicants add their area of research; PhD applicants confirm an MS thesis and upload a research proposal. Tick the undertaking box and press Submit; an application not submitted is not considered. The system emails a confirmation and the status shows on the dashboard. The introduction page says the deadline for online applications was extended to 5 July 2026.

application_steps.title: Sit the HEC scholarship test
application_steps.detail: Registered candidates take a scholarship test that HEC organises together with the Pakistan High Commission in Colombo and the Sri Lankan Ministry of Higher Education. The test date is not stated.

application_steps.title: Interview in Colombo for shortlisted candidates
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted candidates are interviewed at the Pakistan High Commission in Colombo, together with the Sri Lankan Ministry of Higher Education.

application_steps.title: Merit ranking
application_steps.detail: The merit score gives 50% to the HEC scholarship test, 30% to academic achievement and 20% to the interview. Selection is purely on merit, after HEC examines the documents the applicant submits. The A-Level grade conversion table is used for Sri Lankan grades.

application_steps.title: Accept the award and get your qualification recognised
application_steps.detail: Successful candidates must provide an Equivalence Certificate from IBCC and HEC. In an earlier round (2022) the notice asked selected candidates to email acceptance by a set date or lose the offer to the next candidate; the current pages do not repeat this. HEC alone decides placement.

application_steps.title: Study in English and serve Sri Lanka afterwards
application_steps.detail: Teaching is in English. Recipients must serve Sri Lanka after completing their education in Pakistan. False or misrepresented information can end the scholarship at any stage.

fetch_problems: The advertisement (a JPEG flyer) was not read because it is an image.
The HEC e-portal itself needs an account, so the real application form was not opened; the form fields come from the HEC user manual.
notes: The user manual is dated January 2020 and gives a BS age limit of 22, while the current terms page says 23. The current page was used.
The 2022 provisional-selection page is from an earlier round and is used only to explain the full/partial award split and the acceptance step; its merit cut-off marks are not copied.
The deadline on the page (5 July 2026) has passed.
The manual says the PhD form asks for a statement that an MS thesis was written; the eligibility page says the same.
Subject names are copied from the Programs Offered PDF in source order, as printed (including its spelling).
